_meta.description: The NIST AI RMF 1.0 core taxonomy (Tables 1-4 of NIST AI 100-1: GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE functions, their categories, and every subcategory). This is TAXONOMY data only, mirroring harmonised_standards.json's catalogue pattern -- it carries no verdict. opencomplai_core.nist_rmf_report re-projects existing EU-AI-Act-native evidence onto this taxonomy via data/framework_crosswalk.json; nothing here is a computed conformity statement.
_meta.source: NIST AI 100-1, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), National Institute of Standards and Technology, January 2023 (public domain, US Government work) -- Tables 1-4 (AI RMF Core). Subcategory codes and outcome text retrieved from NIST's public AIRC site (https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/airmf/5-sec-core/ and the companion /airmf-resources/playbook/{govern,map,measure,manage}/ pages) at researched_at.
_meta.pending_revision_caveat: As of researched_at, AI RMF 1.0 (Jan 2023) remains NIST's current published core -- no revised core table exists yet. The White House 'America's AI Action Plan' (2025-07-23) directed NIST to revise the AI RMF to remove references to misinformation, diversity/equity/inclusion, and climate change; that revision was still in process, not published, as of researched_at. GOVERN 3 (workforce diversity/equity/inclusion, both subcategories) and MEASURE 2.12 (environmental impact/sustainability) are the subcategories most likely to be altered or removed by that directive. Flagged here for founder/legal re-verification independent of the per-row needs_founder_review the coverage rule (nist_rmf_report.py) already carries on every computed verdict -- this caveat is about the taxonomy itself going stale, not about a mapping being uncertain.
_meta.text_fidelity_note: Outcome text below was retrieved via an automated fetch/summarization step against NIST's own public site, not transcribed by a human directly from the primary NIST AI 100-1 PDF byte-for-byte. A human reviewer should diff each subcategory's outcome text against the primary publication before this file is relied on as a verbatim citation source; the subcategory codes and function/category structure (which is what the coverage rule actually keys on) were independently cross-checked against two separate fetches and the known public total of 72 subcategories, and are considered reliable.
